title: Capability Catalog Schema
body:
This Signature record covers Capability Catalog Schema within the Tool Selection and Capability Registry Signature Database. Maps tasks to available tools, APIs, programs, and generators. It is Manon's original design for this topic, written for the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source.

How it works. Registry method: each tool declares its capabilities, inputs, costs, and limits, and matching ranks candidates against the task requirements. The Signature version keeps the same honest structure as the public record: stated inputs, a repeatable procedure, stated outputs, and explicit limits. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the simple rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Signature framing. Manon's original Signature registry designs: capability catalogs and tool matching inside the Signature ecosystem.

Scope and limits. This record describes Manon's original designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how capability catalog schema is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.
demo_code:
# Capability Catalog Schema: tool ranking by capability minus cost
tools = [('alpha', 8, 2), ('beta', 7, 3), ('gamma', 9, 4)]
ranked = sorted(tools, key=lambda t: t[1] - t[2], reverse=True)
for name, cap, cost in ranked:
    print(name, 'score:', cap - cost)
demo_output:
alpha score: 6
gamma score: 5
beta score: 4

title: Capability Gap Reporting
body:
This Signature record covers Capability Gap Reporting within the Tool Selection and Capability Registry Signature Database. Maps tasks to available tools, APIs, programs, and generators. It is Manon's original design for this topic, written for the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source.

How it works. Registry method: each tool declares its capabilities, inputs, costs, and limits, and matching ranks candidates against the task requirements. The Signature version keeps the same honest structure as the public record: stated inputs, a repeatable procedure, stated outputs, and explicit limits. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the most-complex rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Signature framing. Manon's original Signature registry designs: capability catalogs and tool matching inside the Signature ecosystem.

Scope and limits. This record describes Manon's original designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how capability gap reporting is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.
demo_code:
# Capability Gap Reporting: tool ranking by capability minus cost
tools = [('alpha', 8, 2), ('beta', 7, 3), ('gamma', 9, 4)]
ranked = sorted(tools, key=lambda t: t[1] - t[2], reverse=True)
for name, cap, cost in ranked:
    print(name, 'score:', cap - cost)
demo_output:
alpha score: 6
gamma score: 5
beta score: 4
